title: Introducing Cedar MCP: build GTM agents around your sales process
summary: Open, composable data, sales intelligence, actions, and rep execution for your GTM plays. See the four layers come together in pipeline revival.
body_markdown:
AI has made it easier to automate work across a sales team. Drafting an email or updating a CRM field is a useful starting point. The bigger opportunity is helping a rep recognize a good opportunity and act on it at the right time.


That takes more than a model and a connection to your inbox. An agent needs to understand the account, recognize what matters to your sales process, use the right tools, and put useful work in front of the person who will carry it forward.


**Cedar MCP makes those pieces available as open, composable modules for GTM systems you build and own.** You can bring Cedar’s context and capabilities into your agents, combine them with your internal systems, and build around the way your team sells.


## Build the plays your sales process needs


The most useful sales workflows are often specific to a business. A promising account at one company might look ordinary at another. The right moment to re-engage a buyer depends on why they stopped talking, what has changed, and whether your team has something relevant to offer.


Those details make a workflow difficult to capture in a fixed sequence of rules. They are also what make an agent worth building.


In the launch film, we describe three examples customers have built with Cedar. An account-scoring model combines product usage, engagement, and conversation data. A Slack-monitoring agent looks for buying signals or friction on accounts the team already owns. A pipeline-revival agent prepares specific, useful outreach with relevant case studies and product updates.


Each play brings different information together. Usage says something about what an account is doing. A conversation explains what the buyer cares about. A product update can change whether an old objection still applies. The agent needs to connect those facts to a next step.


Cedar MCP provides the shared foundation for this work. Your team can focus on the judgment and workflow that make the play useful for your business.


## 1. Start with a unified data layer


An agent’s first challenge is finding the right context. A CRM record may describe the current stage of an opportunity, while the reason a buyer hesitated lives in an earlier conversation. An internal system may hold usage data that helps explain whether the account is becoming more engaged.


Cedar’s data layer brings sales context together and extracts structured information that agents can query. That structure makes it possible to narrow a question before reading all the underlying detail.


For example, an agent looking for revival opportunities needs more than a list of closed-lost deals. It needs to find the ones where a particular change could matter: a product gap has been addressed, a competitor timeline is approaching, or the buyer’s stated timing has become relevant again. Structured queries help identify the candidates; the conversation history explains whether the match makes sense.


The advantage is reusable context. Each new agent can start from the same account history instead of requiring a rep to assemble it again. Teams can also combine that history with the information in their own systems.


Openness is central to this layer. Cedar lets you query and export your data and make it available to your internal agents. You can use the foundation through Cedar’s product or incorporate it into a workflow you maintain.[Explore the data layer](https://mail.cedarcopilot.com/platform/data) for a closer look at how sales context is organized.


## 2. Add intelligence about how you sell


Finding a relevant fact is the start of a decision. The agent still needs to understand what that fact means for your team.


Cedar’s sales-intelligence layer combines foundational sales knowledge with the specifics of your sales process. It gives agents context for interpreting an opportunity, choosing useful work, and deciding what deserves a rep’s attention.


Consider account scoring. High activity alone does not explain whether a deal is promising. A busy conversation could be a strong evaluation, or it could be a discussion about a blocker your product cannot resolve. The meaning comes from the details of the conversation and how they relate to your process.


The same applies to pipeline revival. A recent product release does not make every old opportunity equally relevant. The agent needs to consider the original fit, the value of the deal, and how compelling the new reason to engage is. This layer helps turn a broad set of possible actions into a more useful set of priorities.


## 3. Give the agent useful actions


Many teams already have agents that draft emails or update CRM fields. Cedar adds capabilities they can compose into more involved plays: Slack and LinkedIn workflows, signals, custom CRM objects, and deep research.


That wider set of tools matters because the next useful step varies by account. One opportunity needs more research before anyone reaches out. Another needs a message on the channel where the relationship already exists. Another needs a better understanding of the buying group before the rep approaches a new stakeholder.


Your agent can use the actions that fit the play and connect them to tools you already have. The workflow can start with the account’s needs and carry those through to a concrete draft, research result, or proposed next step.


MCP provides the interface for making supported tools and context available to a connected assistant. The tools available to a particular workflow depend on its connections and permissions. Our[Cedar MCP guide](https://mail.cedarcopilot.com/blog/cedar-mcp-sales-context) explains the connection paths in more detail.


## 4. Make the work usable by the rep


An agent’s output only becomes useful when someone can act on it. A recommendation without its context leaves the rep to reconstruct the reasoning before taking the next step.


Cedar’s rep-execution layer provides shared task infrastructure across Slack, Claude, and Cedar’s own UI. The goal is to bring the work and the relevant context into the places where the team already operates.


For a rep, that can mean receiving a timely Slack notification and opening a single place with the account history, the reason the opportunity matters now, and the work the agent has prepared. The rep can assess the next step with the evidence in front of them.


This layer connects the rest of the system to the team’s daily work. Data makes the opportunity understandable. Intelligence helps prioritize it. Tools prepare an action. The workspace makes that action usable.


## Put the layers together: pipeline revival


The launch closes with a concrete example of all four layers working together.


### Preserve why the deal happened—and why it stopped


Cedar builds context around the opportunity: why the buyer took the call, who the team spoke with, the buyer’s pain points and objections, and why the deal did not close. That history gives a revival agent a specific starting point.


A buyer who was waiting for a missing capability needs a different reason to reconnect from one whose timing was wrong. Preserving that distinction is what lets the agent prepare a relevant approach later.


### Watch for a reason to revisit it


In the revival workflow, Owl, Cedar’s watcher, tracks changes that could make a lost deal worth revisiting. Those changes can include product updates captured through changelogs and sales calls, as well as signals such as competitor timelines.


The agent can connect a new event to the original conversation. A release becomes useful when it addresses the concern that held this particular buyer back. A timeline becomes useful when it creates a credible reason to talk now.


### Prioritize and prepare the next step


The sales-intelligence layer helps score the opportunities for revival fit, combining the quality of the original deal, its value, and the strength of the current reason to engage. That gives the rep a way to prioritize their attention.


The action layer can then prepare an email, LinkedIn message, or Slack message. It can also do deeper research or investigate whether another stakeholder would be useful to involve. The outreach follows from the account’s history and the new information.


Finally, the rep receives a Slack ping and a single place in Cedar with the context they need. The full workflow carries the opportunity from an old conversation to a timely, reviewable next step.


## Build on the pieces that matter to your team


Cedar MCP opens up the infrastructure behind these plays so teams can build their own. The same layers can support account scoring, account monitoring, revival, or another workflow shaped by your sales process.
